title: Can we tile a five by three grid with a middle square removed?
description: A grid of five rows and three columns has the middle square of its second row removed. Fourteen squares are left, so seven tiles are needed. Working round the hole one square at a time gives a tiling. Keeko's doubt, that a hole in the middle blocks it, is struck.
teaching_notes: One idea: cover the squares next to the hole first, then fill the rest. Watch for students who think a hole in the middle makes tiling impossible.

source: A 5 × 3 grid has the middle square of its second row removed
video_script.why: The child sees that a grid with a hole in the middle can still be tiled by working round the hole.
video_script.substitution: The squares next to the hole are paired with their neighbours first, then the full rows below are filled with upright tiles.
video_script.anchor: A grid of unit squares with 5 rows and 3 columns, the middle square of its second row removed, and a tile that covers 2 squares.
video_script.wrong_answer: a hole in the middle blocks it
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a hole in the middle blocks it. But fourteen is even, so the count gives no reason to stop, and we can work round the hole one square at a time.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, a tiling with seven tiles exists.

final_answer.value: Yes: a tiling with 7 tiles exists
final_answer.spoken: yes, a tiling with seven tiles exists

maths_rules: The grid has 5 × 3 = 15 squares, and 1 is removed, so 14 are left, and 14 ÷ 2 = 7 tiles are needed.
Row 1: the left two squares form one horizontal tile.
The top right square goes with the square below it: one vertical tile.
The left square of row 2 goes with the left square of row 3: one vertical tile.
The middle and right squares of row 3 form one horizontal tile.
Rows 4 and 5: one vertical tile in each of the 3 columns, 3 tiles.
4 tiles above and 3 tiles below make 7 tiles, with no gaps and no overlaps.
Slip: a hole in the middle does not block a tiling; work round it one square at a time.
video_script.design: One grid with a hole in the middle of the second row. The squares next to the hole are paired first. The slip is thinking the hole stops everything.
